_comment: can-tools, whose canbench/ is the CAN adapter package gen-inhibit uses (vehicle_runner.py's --interface auto, and the tester's Kvaser opener in the bench harness), at one commit (AGENTS.md, "can-tools"; user, 2026-10-30: each project pins its own can-tools and moves the pin itself; the pin is the implementor's, reviewer 2026-10-30 and 2026-11-11; moving it before a bench case where the PCAN witnesses under jammer bursts is the tester's call, reviewer 2026-11-12). can_tools_pin.py writes that commit's canbench/ out of the CAN_TOOLS_DIR clone into the worktree's scratch/can-tools/<commit>/ and refuses any other canbench. fa6c0ae (2026-11-11) adds canbench.live.linux_fixes, without which no Kvaser channel opens on Linux. 5e30066 (2026-11-13, from fa6c0ae, the tester before the jammer-idf bench pass, reviewer 2026-11-13) adds errors.py and the canbench pcan/kvaser classes, the PCAN's bus-off recovery (PCAN_HARD_RESET_STATUS) and the Kvaser's polled state, all reached only through canbench.live.backends.install(), and FrameClock in receiver/can_logger; linux_fixes.py is unchanged. 5952c0c (2026-11-18, from 5e30066, asked for by the gen-inhibit reviewer's Kvaser ruling of 2026-11-18, relayed by the tester) adds canbench.live.socketcan_hw.SocketcanHwBus, a SocketCAN bus that keeps the adapter's hardware stamps beside the host stamps, with a per-open stamp check, through which the bench harness's kvaser_bus opens the Kvaser on Linux; between the two commits receiver's reconnect opens through canbench.buses.open_bus, detection logs at INFO the channels of an asked brand that did not open, and the replay, parser and trcwriter modules change; linux_fixes.py is unchanged. 5220d37 (2026-11-18, from 5952c0c, the gen-inhibit reviewer 2026-11-18) adds canbench.bench_roles, the canbench half of shared/bench SPEC section 8 from shared tag 2026.11.18.2 (a tool asks for a bench adapter by its canctl role): resolve(role) and open_role(role, bitrate=, modes=, hw_timestamps=), which applies linux_fixes and releases a libusb gs_usb role on shutdown, read through canctl roles (read-only, no root); on a host with canctl, receiver's detect_all_can_interfaces adds role:<role> to the ids and the description of each adapter a role resolves to, and replay names why an unmatched role: pin did not match; linux_fixes.py, socketcan_hw.py and receiver's Adapter are unchanged. ec7cefe (2026-11-19, from 5220d37, the gen-inhibit reviewer 2026-11-19) adds canbench.bench_layer, the bench-role layer both ESP projects share: set_guard (the bench guard a caller plugs in; with none set, nothing on the bench is touched), link_up/link_down through sudo -n canctl, each read back with ip -details -json, set_mode/to_libusb/to_socketcan, open_bench (the role brought to the caller's mode or DEFAULT_MODES, a SocketCAN link brought up, then bench_roles.open_role; put back as found on shutdown and on a failed open unless restore=False), refuse_picks, and bus_error/bus_error_class (on SocketCAN only the bus-error classes count); and canbench.bench_scan, the adapter-open scan merged from both projects' scans (ast only, nothing imported or run), with self_check; bench_roles.py, linux_fixes.py, socketcan_hw.py, errors.py and receiver's Adapter are unchanged. 0f9c85f (2026-11-19, from ec7cefe, the gen-inhibit reviewer's three bench_layer items) changes bench_layer and bench_roles: a set_mode or link_up that fails inside open_bench (such as a mode move that did not settle, or a bad link read-back) puts the role back to its found mode and link, a half-moved one included (386e01f); open_bench(if_up="refuse") refuses a role found with its link up before touching anything, and the default if_up="take" works as before (386e01f); open_bench(drain=True), for a libusb gs_usb role only, runs a reader thread that counts echoes, rx and errors into bus.bench_drain, with recv refused while it runs, and bus.stop_drain() returns the counts (shutdown() stops it before the device closes), since the device stops taking sends after 257 unread TX echoes (0f9c85f); and open_role's libusb gs_usb bus honours send(msg, timeout) as pyusb's write timeout for that send, 0 taken as 1 ms and None keeping 1 s (0f9c85f). No file is added; linux_fixes.py, socketcan_hw.py, errors.py, bench_scan.py and receiver's Adapter are unchanged.
